claims.claim: The main risk is memory on a 512 MB VM, not language choice
claims.measured: java-spring peak memory 220–500 MB across tests (499 MB single-query DB, 500 MB 20-query DB, 491 MB I/O wait) in a 512 MB container; idle 134 MB
claims.why: Spring Boot's measured peak memory reaches about 500 MB of the 512 MB limit under load, so memory really is the tight constraint.

claims.claim: 200 small writes per second is a modest workload... Most of the work is HTTP handling and JDBC, which Java does well
claims.measured: java-spring 7,668 req/s single-row DB query (java-spring-vt 12,731); 1,254 req/s even with 20 queries per request, on 1 CPU
claims.why: Measured Spring Boot database throughput on 1 CPU is far above 200 requests/s, so this load is modest for it.

claims.claim: Quarkus or Micronaut typically use noticeably less memory than Spring Boot on the JVM, and can produce native images
claims.why: Neither Quarkus nor Micronaut was benchmarked.

claims.claim: Go, Rust, or Node: lighter at runtime
claims.measured: Peak memory: Go 7–16 MB, Rust 3–10 MB, Node 55–77 MB vs Spring Boot 209–500 MB; idle memory 1–43 MB vs 131–134 MB
claims.why: All three used several times less memory than Spring Boot in every test, so they are lighter.

claims.claim: On a 512 MB VM the kernel can kill the JVM under load without a clean Java error
claims.measured: java-spring peak 499–500 MB in the database tests under a 512 MB limit
claims.why: Measured peak resident memory came within a few MB of the 512 MB limit, so an OOM kill under load is a realistic risk.
